result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): The two answers cover nearly the same ground: both put the moves counter first, suggest 52px tiles, move power-ups into the empty space and do the same space math. B is slightly ahead because it ends with a top-to-bottom layout, gives the low-moves warning its own item, and shows how to tell locked power-ups apart from used-up ones (padlock vs. a '0' badge or '+'). A labels each problem by severity more clearly and adds a useful 'Keep' list, but its layout advice is a little less concrete. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers find the same core problems and give similar concrete fixes: a bigger, higher-contrast moves counter, a labeled goal bar, power-up counts and lock icons, power-ups moved to the thumb zone, and 52px tiles. B edges ahead because each finding has an explicit severity label (blocker, major, minor), it quantifies the combined dead space (about 340px), and it adds a 'Keep' list and a quick playtest check. A's strengths are its suggested top-to-bottom layout and a separate item on the low-moves warning, but its layout-balance analysis comes later and feels less integrated.
